name: RedFoxtrot
affiliation_detail:
Recorded Future's Insikt Group identified "specific ties" between RedFoxtrot and PLA Unit 69010 "with high confidence." The connection stemmed from "lax operational security measures" by a suspected RedFoxtrot operator, whose online persona disclosed the physical address of Unit 69010 and had a history of affiliation with the PLA's Communications Command Academy in Wuhan. (Recorded Future, 2021)
The unit is located in Ürümqi, Xinjiang, and its operational remit aligns with RedFoxtrot's targeting of Central Asia, South Asia, and bordering countries — regions directly relevant to China's western border security, Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) infrastructure, and counterterrorism interests in Xinjiang. (Recorded Future, 2021)
No individuals have been indicted.
description:
RedFoxtrot is a PLA-linked cyber espionage group active since at least 2014, attributed by Recorded Future with high confidence to PLA Unit 69010 based in Ürümqi, Xinjiang. The group predominantly targets government, defense, telecommunications, aerospace, mining, and research organizations across Central Asia, South Asia, and China's western border countries. (Recorded Future, 2021)
In 2022, SentinelLabs documented overlapping activity under the name "Moshen Dragon," targeting Central Asian telecom providers. Moshen Dragon was notable for systematically abusing security vendor software — from Symantec, TrendMicro, BitDefender, McAfee, and Kaspersky — to sideload ShadowPad and PlugX variants via DLL search order hijacking. SentinelLabs noted the overlap with RedFoxtrot and Nomad Panda but did not make a definitive merge. (SentinelLabs, 2022) 
In Relation to SentinelLabs report, it is worth departing slightly from  the otherwise descriptive purpose of this project and insert a one-sentence note. Coincidence that PLA Unit 61419 (Tick) procured all of this software a year earlier? (see Tick: Recoded Future, 2021) 
Broadcom's April 2025 "Relentless Force" report reported continued activity, tracking the group as Needleminer and documenting use of the Quickheal backdoor with updated configuration and VMProtect obfuscation — "almost identical to Quickheal variants documented by Recorded Future in 2021." (Broadcom, 2025) The group has operated alongside Naikon and other Chinese groups in coordinated campaigns against Southeast Asian telecoms. (Broadcom, 2025)

campaigns.name: India-Focused Espionage (Galwan Tensions)
campaigns.description: Recorded Future documented a six-month period in which RedFoxtrot showed "a particular focus on Indian targets, which occurred at a time of heightened border tensions between India and the People's Republic of China" following the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash. Intrusions targeted three Indian aerospace and defense contractors, major telecom providers in India, and government agencies. The group used Icefog, PlugX, Royal Road, and Poison Ivy for initial access and persistence. (Recorded Future, 2021)

campaigns.name: Central Asian Telecom Targeting (Moshen Dragon)
campaigns.description: SentinelLabs documented Chinese-aligned cyberespionage targeting the telecommunications sector in Central Asia under the Moshen Dragon designation. The group deployed five DLL sideloading triads abusing security vendor software — including Symantec, TrendMicro, BitDefender, McAfee, and Kaspersky products — to load ShadowPad and PlugX variants. Additional tools included an LSA notification package for credential harvesting and the GUNTERS passive backdoor. Activity partially overlaps with RedFoxtrot and Nomad Panda. (SentinelLabs, 2022)

campaigns.name: Central and South Asian Government and Telecom Intrusions
campaigns.description: Beyond India, Recorded Future documented RedFoxtrot intrusions against major telecommunications providers in Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, and Pakistan, and multiple government agencies across Central Asia. The targeting aligns with the operational remit of PLA Unit 69010 and Chinese strategic interests in Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure and western border security. (Recorded Future, 2021)
